vulnerability_analysis: The TetherToken contract has owner-only functions that allow arbitrary token seizure from blacklisted addresses. The owner can blacklist any address and then call destroyBlackFunds() to transfer all tokens from that address to the owner. Since the attacker can become the owner through transferOwnership(), they can abuse this privilege to seize tokens from themselves, effectively increasing their balance.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the current owner to transfer ownership to ourselves, then use owner privileges to blacklist our own address and seize our tokens to the owner (which is now us), resulting in net balance increase.
step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate current owner using vm.prank
2. Call transferOwnership() to make attacker the new owner
3. Use deal() to give attacker some USDT tokens
4. As new owner, call addBlackList() to blacklist attacker address
5. Call destroyBlackFunds() on attacker address to seize tokens to owner
6. Verify attacker balance increased
